teks.statement: Learning Greek and Latin word parts is not itself a science TEKS. These activities support students' access to TEKS-aligned science content by making unfamiliar science vocabulary decodable. Exact TEKS codes will be added only after verification against the current TEA standards.

ngss.statement: Morphology is not an NGSS Performance Expectation. These activities support the literacy demands of science learning — obtaining, evaluating, and communicating information, and using patterns and structure-and-function language. Specific Performance Expectations will be listed only where the alignment is defensible and has been checked.

sst.statement: Beginning in 2027–2028, the Student Success Tool replaces STAAR in Texas with beginning-, middle-, and end-of-year assessments. The BOY / MOY / EOY progression used on this site is a local instructional approach for SST readiness. It is not a TEA requirement, and nothing here is an official or approved SST item.

checkpoints.label: BOY
checkpoints.demand: Recognize a word part and say what clue it gives.

checkpoints.label: MOY
checkpoints.demand: Combine word structure with science evidence and explain why they fit.

checkpoints.label: EOY
checkpoints.demand: Use known word parts to interpret an unfamiliar term or situation and justify it with evidence.
